problem_context.topic: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
problem_context.source: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 3 Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables, Exercise 3.3, Q2 (ii) (p. 36)

glossary.definition: A variable is a letter for a number we do not know yet. Example: let A's age be a years.
A linear equation in two variables looks like ax + by = c, with no x², y² or xy. Example: 2x + 3y = 12.
Two linear equations in the same two variables, solved together. Example: x + y = 7 and x − y = 1 have the solution x = 4, y = 3.
Add or subtract the equations (after multiplying if needed) so one variable disappears. Example: (x + y) + (x − y) = 7 + 1 gives 2x = 8, so x = 4.
Write one variable from one equation and put it into the other. Example: x + y = 7 gives x = 7 − y; then (7 − y) − y = 1, so y = 3.
Thrice means three times. Example: if B is 4, a number thrice as big is 3 × 4 = 12.
Twice means two times. Example: if B is 6, a number twice as big is 2 × 6 = 12.
'n years ago' means take n away from today's age. Example: A is a years old now, so 3 years ago A was a − 3.
'n years later' means add n to today's age. Example: A is a years old now, so in 4 years A will be a + 4.

nodes.label: A: Elimination
nodes.description: Subtract the equations to remove x

nodes.label: B: Substitution
nodes.description: x = 3y − 10, put it into the other equation

nodes.label: Solve the Pair
nodes.prompt: Now solve the pair of equations by the elimination method.
hints: Solve the pair: subtract the equations to remove x (elimination). Example: x + y = 7 and x − y = 1: (x + y) − (x − y) = 7 − 1 gives 2y = 6, so y = 3.
Then put that value back into either equation. Example: 2x + 2 = 9, so x = 3.5.

conditions: five years ago, Nuri was thrice as old as Sonu
ten years later, Nuri will be twice as old as Sonu
ask: How old were Nuri (x) and Sonu (y) five years ago, and which is three times the other?
How old will Nuri (x) and Sonu (y) be ten years later, and which is two times the other?
relation_next: Now use the same idea for five years ago: their ages then were x − 5 and y − 5.
Now use the same idea for ten years later: their ages then will be x + 10 and y + 10.

m1: Look at the coefficients of x in the two equations. Are they the same? Then subtract one equation from the other. Example: (2x + y) − (2x − 3y) = 9 − 1 gives 4y = 8, so y = 2.
Then put that value back into either equation. Example: 2x + 2 = 9, so x = 3.5.
m2: Write x from one equation and put it into the other. Example: x − y = 1 gives x = y + 1; then (y + 1) + y = 7, so y = 3.
Then put that value back. Example: x = 3 + 1 = 4.

nodes.prompt: Verify: do your ages fit both sentences of the question?
hints: Put your ages back into the sentences. Example: A = 10 and B = 4, 'two years ago A was four times B': 10 − 2 = 8 and 4 − 2 = 2, and 8 = 4 × 2 ✓.
